title: Private upgrade: chart values for backup targets/retention + feature-flagged rollback hooks (safe defaults)
author: Ines Carvalho
release_notes: - Private Helm charts: add values for backup destination/targets/retention used by installer-driven upgrades; add feature-flagged rollback hook resources/annotations. Defaults are no-op for existing installs.
body:
Summary
Adds explicit, documented Helm values for (a) backup configuration (targets + retention) and (b) rollback hooks, guarded behind a feature flag. This is part of the Private upgrade/rollback work so the installer and SRE runbooks have a consistent contract for what can be configured via charts.

Key goals
- Provide a stable values schema for where upgrade backups land (destination) and how long they’re retained.
- Allow enabling rollback hooks (pre/post hooks, pod annotations, optional Jobs) in a controlled way.
- Ensure defaults are safe for existing installs: no new resources, no new Jobs/hooks, no behavior changes unless explicitly enabled.

What changed
1) Backup values contract (no-op by default)
- Introduces a new values subtree used by the upgrade workflow:
  - privateUpgrade.backup.enabled (default: false)
  - privateUpgrade.backup.destination (default: unset; required if enabled)
  - privateUpgrade.backup.targets (default: ["controlPlaneDb", "configState"] but only acted on if enabled)
  - privateUpgrade.backup.retention (default: {"days": 7, "maxSnapshots": 14} but only acted on if enabled)
- The chart does NOT start doing backups automatically in this PR. These values are consumed by the upgrade orchestration components (installer + upgrade Jobs/hooks introduced in ENG-2320) and surfaced as ConfigMap data + annotations so the orchestration layer can read a single source of truth.

2) Feature-flagged rollback hooks
- Adds privateUpgrade.rollbackHooks.enabled (default: false)
- When enabled:
  - Adds stable annotations to Deployments/StatefulSets that the installer/upgrade controller uses as rollback boundaries.
  - Adds an optional pre-upgrade/pre-rollback hook Job template (disabled by default) for components that need ordering guarantees.
- When disabled (default): no new annotations that change behavior, and no new Jobs/hooks are created.

3) Docs + schema updates
- Updates chart README with the new values, including examples for VPC (S3-compatible object store) and on-prem (filesystem/NFS).
- Updates values.schema.json to validate types and enforce that destination is set when backup.enabled=true.

Implementation details
- The new values are mostly surfaced via a ConfigMap "redwood-private-upgrade-config" and per-component annotations.
- All templates are wrapped in conditionals:
  - {{- if .Values.privateUpgrade.backup.enabled }} ... {{- end }}
  - {{- if .Values.privateUpgrade.rollbackHooks.enabled }} ... {{- end }}
- The hook Job is intentionally conservative:
  - activeDeadlineSeconds set
  - backoffLimit low
  - uses the same imagePullSecrets/serviceAccount as existing admin jobs

Illustrative snippet
values.yaml
privateUpgrade:
  backup:
    enabled: false
    destination:
      type: "" # s3|filesystem (required if enabled)
      bucket: "" # required for s3
      prefix: "" # optional
      path: ""   # required for filesystem
    targets:
      - controlPlaneDb
      - configState
    retention:
      days: 7
      maxSnapshots: 14
  rollbackHooks:
    enabled: false

templates/control-plane-deployment.yaml (excerpt)
{{- if .Values.privateUpgrade.rollbackHooks.enabled }}
metadata:
  annotations:
    redwood.ai/upgrade-boundary: "control-plane"
    redwood.ai/rollback-hook: "enabled"
{{- end }}

Safety / backwards compatibility
- Default behavior is unchanged:
  - backup.enabled defaults to false
  - rollbackHooks.enabled defaults to false
  - no new resources created by default
- Schema validation only becomes strict when backup.enabled=true (destination required). Existing installations with default values remain valid.

Test plan
- chart-testing (ct lint + install) on kind cluster
- helm template diff against previous release values (no-op default) verified locally
- Added/updated unit tests for template conditionals to ensure no resources render when flags are disabled

Checklist
- [x] Defaults do not alter behavior for existing installs
- [x] values.schema.json updated
- [x] README/examples updated
- [x] ct lint + install passes
- [x] Reviewed hook Job timeouts / failure behavior with SRE

Links
- ENG-2317 (backup primitive)
- ENG-2318 (rollback hooks contract)
- ENG-2320 (upgrade sequencing via Helm hooks)

Commits
- charts(private): add privateUpgrade.backup values + schema validation
- charts(private): add feature-flagged rollback hook annotations and optional hook job
- docs(charts): document backup destination/retention and rollback hook flags
- tests(charts): add template unit tests for conditional resources

Review conversation (highlights)
- Ethan Park: “Can we guarantee this doesn’t render any extra resources by default? We’ve been burned by ‘harmless’ ConfigMaps showing up and triggering reconciles.”
  - Ines Carvalho: “Yep—ConfigMap + hook Job are behind privateUpgrade.backup.enabled / rollbackHooks.enabled. With defaults, the rendered manifests are identical to main (verified with helm template + diff). Added a unit test that asserts no upgrade ConfigMap is rendered unless enabled.”

- Sean Gallagher: “Retention knobs: do we want both days and maxSnapshots? Also ensure we don’t imply the chart is enforcing retention.”
  - Ines Carvalho: “Agreed. Clarified wording in README: chart only publishes configuration; retention enforcement is done by the installer backup step. Kept both fields since different backends (filesystem vs object store) will implement enforcement differently; installer can decide precedence.”

- Marcus Lin: “Destination config: please avoid encouraging static credentials in values.yaml. Can we steer users toward IRSA / workload identity and existing secret refs?”
  - Ines Carvalho: “Updated examples to use secretRef + IAM role approach and added a warning note. Also ensured we only reference existing secrets and do not create any secret resources in this chart.”

- Connor O’Brien: “Make sure these names align with what the installer expects; otherwise we’ll have ‘two sources of truth’.”
  - Ines Carvalho: “Aligned key names to the installer draft contract (privateUpgrade.backup.* and privateUpgrade.rollbackHooks.*). Added a short mapping note in README that this is the contract consumed by redwood-private-installer upgrade plan.”

CI / Checks
- buildkite/redwood-helm-charts: ct-lint ✅
- buildkite/redwood-helm-charts: ct-install ✅
- buildkite/redwood-helm-charts: helm-unittest ✅
- buildkite/redwood-helm-charts: yamllint ✅ (initially failed on line length in README example; fixed in 5b7a0c2)

Merge
- Merged via squash into main on 2025-01-23.
- Follow-up: installer wiring to consume these values lives in ENG-2317/ENG-2320 PRs; this PR is intentionally non-functional without those components enabled.
